explanation: After the earlier reductions in the Ax–Schanuel proof, the image $\pi_{Y(1)^n}U$ is algebraic and is not contained in a proper weakly special subvariety. The authors invoke the monodromy theorem of André and Deligne to obtain Zariski density in $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})^n$. A finite-index property of the induced fundamental-group map carries this density to the jet-space setting. The analytic set $U$ is invariant under a Zariski-dense subgroup. Its algebraic closure $V=U^{\mathrm{Zar}}$, rather than necessarily $U$ itself, is consequently invariant under the full algebraic group. The action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ on $J_2\mathbb{P}^1\setminus J_2^0\mathbb{P}^1$ is transitive. This identifies the fibers of the projection from $V$ to the relevant jet space as $J_2\mathbb{C}^n$, of dimension $3n$, completing the dimension argument within the theorem’s stated setting.
limits: Full-group invariance is asserted for the algebraic closure V; invariance under a dense subgroup does not by itself give the same assertion for an arbitrary analytic U.
